text:
maya: heads up — SLO alert just fired for hosted-infer prod-usw1, p99 5xx jump starting ~02:12 UTC. seeing lots of 502/504 from gateway. anyone already digging? :eyes:
jon: i'm on it, joining. do we have customer reports?
support-bot: escalation created: #CS-7281 — customer 'AcmeRetail' reporting 502s since ~02:15 UTC, samples attached.
maya: thanks. quick glance at grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ABCD/ingress-overview?var-region=usw1 shows p99 spike and a corresponding increase in gateway upstream_errors.
observability-bot: SLO alert detail: slo=ingress_p99_requests, window=15m, burn=420%.
tara: running a logs query now: `logs query: service:gateway | where status >= 500 | stats count() by upstream, message | sort -count`
tara: results: upstream=billing-proxy ~1200, upstream=model-router ~180, common message: "upstream reset by peer" and "connection timed out".
jon: hmm billing-proxy dominating. i also see a trace gap in many requests — traces start at gateway and then nothing from gateway->billing-proxy span. possible tracer agent restart or sampling config changed.
maya: i pulled a few raw request IDs from the customer samples and ran `span search` — a lot of them end at the gateway client send with no downstream spans.
oliver: i saw a similar pattern earlier in another region when the token-exchange service dropped keepalive and closed connections. could be retry storms.
jon: can someone paste the curl repro we used? trying to hit billing-proxy token endpoint with same headers.
maya: repro curl (redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -X POST https://gateway.prod-usw1.redwood.ai/v1/infer -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
maya: when run repeatedly from ci-runner, ~1/5 requests return 502 with `upstream reset by peer`.
tara: raw logs snippet: `2026-03-17T02:17:34Z gateway INFO req=abcd status=502 upstream=billing-proxy msg="write tcp: connection reset by peer"`
jon: i'm going to open a quick bypass route to avoid billing-proxy for customer canaries (route -> billing-proxy-bypass) and see if that stabilizes. can we get approvals?
maya: +1 for temporary bypass for impacted customers. pinging @oliver for infra ACL change. :pray:
oliver: applying route change now (will only affect 5% traffic). rolling out in 30s.
observability-bot: deploy started: canary-route-bypass (5% traffic) — link: https://deploys.redwood.com/runs/8342
maya: after canary apply p99 down to baseline in the canary cohort. non-canary still high.
tara: i ran a more focused logs query against billing-proxy instances: `logs query: service:billing-proxy | where status >= 500 | stats count() by instance, error_type` — instance bp-3 shows 95% of errors and high tcp close rates.
jon: paging eng-infra to check bp-3 health and kernel logs. @oliver can you check kernel OOM/conntrack?
oliver: bp-3 shows many TIME_WAIT and resets, but no OOM. kernel logs show: `tcp: too many orphaned sockets` around 02:10 — looks like connection handling overwhelmed.
maya: that aligns with a recent config change: billing-proxy env `KEEPALIVE_MAX=50` was accidentally lowered in last deploy at 01:50. can we revert?
jon: rolling rollback of billing-proxy config to previous KEEPALIVE_MAX=500 now. applying to all instances.
ara: (typo) that was tara actually, corrected.
tara: rollback applied at 02:28 UTC, monitoring...
maya: within 3 minutes p95/p99 error rates started declining. can still see a few stragglers (in-flight retry windows).
support-bot: note added to CS ticket #CS-7281 — root cause: billing-proxy keepalive misconfiguration caused connection churn and upstream resets. rollback applied, partial mitigation: bypass route for affected customers.
jon: follow-ups: 1) add automated pre-deploy check for critical conn config (KEEPALIVE_MAX), 2) add alert for orphaned socket rate > threshold, 3) add tracing heartbeat to ensure spans continue through proxy.
maya: i'll file an RFC for config validation and add runbook steps for bypass route and rollback. tagging eng-releases to prevent regressions.
oliver: system metrics back to normal at 02:40 UTC in prod-usw1. last observed 5xx after rollback at 02:36.
jon: closing thread — watchers please keep an eye for 2 hours and escalate if anything resurfaces. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks all, great quick work.
